name: Ptitim rosé risotto — optimized (ריזוטו פתיתים רוזה, גרסה ממוטבת)

source.author: Optimized version of ptitim_rose_risotto_cottage
source.notes: Optimized version of ptitim_rose_risotto_cottage, adopted per user request (the original stays as reference). Changes: whole-wheat/spelt ptitim cut to 400 g, cottage 3% instead of 5%, yellow cheese 150→100 g, olive oil halved, plain passata instead of jarred sauce, NO added salt, plus 250 g mushrooms, 200 g zucchini and 200 g spinach, finished with lemon zest + basil. 8 servings. Vegetarian version. Estimate.

ingredients.note: down from 500 g white ptitim — more fibre, better protein ratio
3% instead of 5% — same protein, less fat
instead of a sweetened jarred sauce
cottage, cheese and parmesan already bring plenty

ingredients.qty: 2 cups to start, up to 1 more as needed

steps: In a wide pot, sauté the mushrooms and zucchini in the olive oil until browned and their liquid has evaporated; add the garlic for 30 sec.
Add the ptitim, cottage, yellow cheese, passata, paprika, pepper and chili flakes. Pour in 2 cups water and stir gently down to the bottom.
Cover and bring to a boil on high, stirring gently now and then; lower to medium-low and cook covered ~8–10 min (whole-wheat ptitim may need a couple of minutes more).
Uncover, stir and add ¼ cup water at a time if needed; cook uncovered ~4–5 min, stirring, until tender and creamy.
Off the heat, fold in the spinach until wilted, add lemon zest and basil, cover 2 min. Taste — add salt only if really needed. Serve with a little parmesan.

batch_totals.note: Whole pot (8 servings), optimized. Vs the original (per serving ~454 kcal / 28.4 g protein / 2.7 g fibre / ~1,173 mg sodium): ~93 kcal less, ~5 g less fat, ~2.5x the fibre, about half the sodium, near-identical protein, plus real folate/iron from spinach.

him.verdict: Keeps the 'protein-packed creamy pasta' idea (~27 g protein per serving) while fixing its weak spots: ~361 kcal instead of ~454, ~6.9 g fibre instead of ~2.7 (whole-wheat ptitim + three vegetables), and sodium roughly halved by dropping the added salt. ~7.5 g protein per 100 kcal, plus lycopene from the tomato.
flags: ~6.9 g fibre — whole-wheat ptitim + mushrooms, zucchini, spinach
suggested_mods: Want more protein? Use the chicken version

her_preconception.verdict: A much better fit for her than the original: spinach adds folate and iron (with vitamin C from tomato and lemon helping absorption), cottage brings protein and calcium, and sodium is halved. Fully cooked, pasteurized cheeses, no safety flags.
prenatal_highlights: folate + iron from spinach (with vitamin C from tomato/lemon for absorption)
high fibre; fully cooked; pasteurized cheeses

adopted_note: Adopted 2026-11-10 (optimized, vegetarian). Per serving (of 8, ~290 g): ~361 kcal, 27.2 g protein, 44.5 g carb, 8.7 g fat, 6.9 g fibre, ~564 mg sodium. him 8 / her 8. Standing spec: 400 g whole-wheat ptitim, 1 kg cottage 3%, 100 g yellow 9%, 1 tbsp olive oil, passata, mushrooms + zucchini + spinach, no added salt, lemon + basil.
cooking_guide: Brown the mushrooms and zucchini first and let their water cook off — this builds flavour (so you need less salt) and stops the risotto going watery.
Use a WIDE pot and stir right down to the base after adding the water; cottage-based sauces catch easily.
Whole-wheat ptitim absorbs a bit more liquid and takes a little longer — add water ¼ cup at a time and taste for tenderness.
Fold the spinach in off the heat; the residual heat wilts it in a minute and keeps its colour and folate.
Finish with lemon zest and fresh basil, then taste before adding any salt — the brightness makes salt mostly unnecessary.
Take it off slightly looser than you want; it thickens on standing. Reheat with a splash of water.
